summary: The input component is the loop's front door for the operator. SelfwareEditor wraps reedline to provide an IDE-like REPL: history-backed, syntax-highlighted, with a Tab-cycling completion menu, Emacs/Vi modes, and keybindings that surface slash commands ('/'), cycle execution mode (Shift+Tab), toggle YOLO (Ctrl+Y), and open an external editor (Ctrl+X). read_line returns a ReadlineResult (Line, Interrupt, Eof, HostCommand). The command_registry catalogs CommandEntry items by CommandCategory and answers is_known_command. On the loop it is the primary perceive source for human intent and the injection point for control signals (mode changes, interrupts) — it turns raw keystrokes into either a task Message or a HostCommand that reshapes the driver.
context_basis: Recommendations formed with input read in the context of the full engine (~600k budget framing), where the REPL feeds the agent loop and ExecuteHostCommand sentinels (__toggle_yolo__, __cycle_mode__) route control changes back into the driver.

examples.title: Read a line as the loop's perceive entry
examples.intent: Capture the operator's request to seed a turn.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: read_line returns ReadlineResult::Line, which becomes the Message that starts the loop's Planning phase; it is the canonical perceive source for human intent.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the input node focuses the on-canvas prompt and raises the soft keyboard.
touch_interaction.visual: The prompt node glows and shows a blinking caret; the typed line renders live.

examples.mini_scenario: The operator types 'refactor the parser' and presses enter; the loop starts a turn from that line.
examples.pitfall: An empty line should be a no-op, not an empty task — filter blanks before starting a turn.

examples.title: Route a HostCommand into loop control
examples.intent: Let keybindings change loop behavior without a task.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Lines wrapped in __sentinels__ return ReadlineResult::HostCommand, which the driver interprets as a control action (mode/YOLO) rather than a Message, mutating loop control directly.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping a control keycap emits its host command into the driver node.
touch_interaction.visual: The command travels as a distinct control-colored pulse, not a normal text bubble.

examples.mini_scenario: Shift+Tab yields '__cycle_mode__'; the loop advances execution mode instead of running a task.
examples.pitfall: Detect sentinels by the __prefix/suffix__ shape — a user literally typing that must be handled deliberately.

examples.title: Complete a command via Tab menu
examples.intent: Speed correct command entry with a cycling menu.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The Tab binding tries hint-complete, inline complete, then opens the columnar menu and cycles — narrowing perceive input to valid commands the loop can act on.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking through the completion menu cycles candidate entries; tapping one accepts it.
touch_interaction.visual: A single-column menu with a ' > ' marker highlights the current pick.

examples.mini_scenario: The operator types 'chec', hits Tab, and the menu offers /checkpoint which they accept.
examples.pitfall: Completion sources must stay in sync with the registry — a stale list offers dead commands.

examples.title: Open the slash-command menu on '/'
examples.intent: Surface commands the instant the user types '/'.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The '/' keybinding inserts the char and immediately opens the completion menu, funneling the operator toward registered CommandEntry actions the loop understands.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the '/' key on the soft keyboard pops the slash-command overlay.
touch_interaction.visual: A menu unfurls under the caret listing slash commands by category.

examples.mini_scenario: Typing '/' shows /undo, /timeline, /stats; the operator taps /stats to inspect the loop.
examples.pitfall: The menu must reflect only known commands — is_known_command should back what it offers.

examples.title: Cycle execution mode with Shift+Tab
examples.intent: Switch how autonomously the loop acts.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Shift+Tab emits __cycle_mode__ to rotate normal → auto-edit → yolo → daemon, changing whether the loop pauses for confirmations at each act.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotating two fingers on the mode node cycles the execution mode ring.
touch_interaction.visual: A ring badge steps color: grey → amber → red → blue as autonomy rises.

examples.mini_scenario: The operator rotates to auto-edit so file edits apply without a per-edit prompt.
examples.pitfall: Landing on yolo removes all confirmations — the UI must make that transition unmistakable.

examples.title: Toggle YOLO with Ctrl+Y
examples.intent: Flip confirmation-free execution on or off.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Ctrl+Y emits __toggle_yolo__; the driver flips the confirmation guard, directly reshaping whether act transitions gate.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the YOLO toggle flips the guard state.
touch_interaction.visual: The toggle snaps red-on / grey-off with a warning pulse when enabling.

examples.mini_scenario: The operator hits Ctrl+Y to enable YOLO for a trusted batch, then again to restore prompts.
examples.pitfall: A stuck YOLO state is dangerous — always reflect the live guard state, never a stale label.

examples.title: Handle Ctrl+C as an interrupt signal
examples.intent: Let the operator abort the current turn.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Signal::CtrlC maps to ReadlineResult::Interrupt, which the driver treats as a cancel, transitioning a running loop toward a clean stop.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the stop node sends an interrupt to the active turn.
touch_interaction.visual: A red stop glyph pulses; the running node winds down to a halted state.

examples.mini_scenario: A long run goes astray; the operator presses Ctrl+C and the loop stops before the next act.
examples.pitfall: Interrupt should cancel gracefully at a safe boundary, not corrupt in-flight state.

examples.title: Handle Ctrl+D as end-of-input
examples.intent: Exit the REPL cleanly.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Signal::CtrlD maps to ReadlineResult::Eof, ending the perceive stream so the loop tears down the session.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking the input node down and off-screen ends the session like an EOF.
touch_interaction.visual: The prompt node slides away and the canvas dims to a closed state.

examples.mini_scenario: The operator presses Ctrl+D on an empty prompt; the loop persists state and exits.
examples.pitfall: Distinguish Eof from Interrupt — Eof ends the session, Interrupt only cancels a turn.

examples.title: Insert a newline with Ctrl+J
examples.intent: Compose multi-line prompts without submitting.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Ctrl+J inserts a newline instead of submitting, letting the operator build a richer Message before the loop consumes it.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping a soft return key adds a line to the prompt without sending it.
touch_interaction.visual: The prompt box grows to accommodate the new line; the caret drops down.

examples.mini_scenario: The operator pastes a multi-line spec using Ctrl+J between lines, then submits it whole.
examples.pitfall: Only Enter submits — don't let a bare newline key double as submit or prompts fragment.

examples.title: Edit the prompt in an external editor
examples.intent: Compose a long prompt in $EDITOR.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Ctrl+X opens the buffer in VISUAL/EDITOR/vi via a temp file, returning the edited text as the loop's next Message.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the input node opens a full-screen editor sheet for the prompt.
touch_interaction.visual: The prompt expands to a full editor pane; on close its content returns to the caret.

examples.mini_scenario: The operator hits Ctrl+X, writes a detailed brief in vim, saves, and the loop receives it.
examples.pitfall: The temp file is per-process — clean it up so stale prompt drafts don't leak.

examples.title: Search history with Ctrl+R
examples.intent: Reuse a previous command from history.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: FileBackedHistory (max 10k) lets the operator recall past lines, so the loop can be re-seeded with a proven prior Message.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking up on the input node scrolls back through history entries.
touch_interaction.visual: Prior commands surface as ghosted suggestions; the match highlights as you refine.

examples.mini_scenario: The operator recalls 'run the e2e suite' from last session and re-submits it.
examples.pitfall: Lines beginning with a space are excluded from history — don't rely on those being recallable.

examples.title: Toggle Emacs/Vi input mode
examples.intent: Match the operator's preferred editing style.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: toggle_vim_mode rebuilds the editor with the other InputMode; it changes how keystrokes are parsed, a foundation choice that doesn't alter loop control.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the mode chip switches between Emacs and Vi editing.
touch_interaction.visual: The chip flips label EMACS/VI; a Vi mode adds a normal/insert indicator.

examples.mini_scenario: A Vi user double-taps to Vi mode and navigates the prompt with hjkl.
examples.pitfall: Rebuilding the editor must preserve history and completers — don't drop them on toggle.

examples.title: Accept an inline hint with Right arrow
examples.intent: Adopt the suggested completion of a line.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Right arrow completes the history hint if present, else moves the cursor — smoothing perceive so common Messages type themselves.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking right on the prompt accepts the ghosted hint completion.
touch_interaction.visual: The dimmed hint solidifies into the line as it is accepted.

examples.mini_scenario: The operator types 'git ' and the hint 'git status' appears; a right-flick accepts it.
examples.pitfall: Right must fall back to cursor-move when there's no hint, or navigation breaks mid-line.

examples.title: Dismiss the menu with Escape
examples.intent: Close a menu without committing a choice.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Esc maps to ReedlineEvent::Esc, closing the completion menu so the operator resumes free input without dispatching a command.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping outside the menu overlay dismisses it without selecting.
touch_interaction.visual: The menu collapses and the caret returns to the unaltered line.

examples.mini_scenario: The operator opens the slash menu by accident and taps away to dismiss it.
examples.pitfall: Esc must not clear the typed line — only the menu; losing the buffer frustrates the operator.

examples.title: Catalog commands by CommandCategory
examples.intent: Organize available commands for discovery.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: command_registry groups CommandEntry by CommandCategory and exposes command_names/description; it is the foundation catalog the perceive layer and palette draw from.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch-out on the registry node fans commands into category clusters.
touch_interaction.visual: Commands group under category headers, each cluster color-coded.

examples.mini_scenario: The palette lists commands grouped as session, safety, and inspection categories.
examples.pitfall: Every offered command must appear in the registry — completions outside it dispatch nothing.

examples.title: Validate a command before dispatch
examples.intent: Reject unknown slash commands cleanly.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: is_known_command gates dispatch so a mistyped '/xyz' is caught at verify rather than becoming a silent no-op or a task.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping an unrecognized command flashes the input node red with a 'not a command' hint.
touch_interaction.visual: The token underlines red; a suggestion of the nearest known command appears.

examples.mini_scenario: The operator types '/undoo'; the gate rejects it and suggests /undo.
examples.pitfall: Don't treat an unknown slash command as a plain task — surface the error instead.

examples.title: Render context in the prompt
examples.intent: Show model, step, and context usage at the prompt.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: set_prompt_full_context updates SelfwarePrompt with model/step/context_pct, so the operator perceives the loop's budget state right where they type.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the prompt chip expands the model/step/context readout.
touch_interaction.visual: The prompt shows 'Qwen3.5 · step 4 · 62%'; the percent tints as it climbs.

examples.mini_scenario: At 88% context the prompt turns amber, nudging the operator to compact before continuing.
examples.pitfall: Keep context_pct fresh — a stale prompt understates real budget pressure.

examples.title: Highlight input syntax live
examples.intent: Give immediate visual structure to what's typed.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: SelfwareHighlighter colors the line as it's entered, improving the fidelity of the perceive channel so the operator catches mistakes before submitting.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the input node toggles syntax highlighting on the live line.
touch_interaction.visual: Commands, paths, and flags render in distinct colors as they're typed.

examples.mini_scenario: A slash command colors differently from a plain task, so the operator sees which they're issuing.
examples.pitfall: Highlighting is cosmetic — never let a color rule change what the command actually does.

examples.title: Seed completer with live tool names
examples.intent: Complete against the actually-registered tools.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: InputConfig.tool_names populates SelfwareCompleter so completion reflects the loop's real tool set, keeping perceive aligned with act capability.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking the completer node refreshes it against the current tool registry.
touch_interaction.visual: Tool suggestions repopulate; newly registered tools appear in the menu.

examples.mini_scenario: After MCP tools register, the completer offers them so the operator can reference them by name.
examples.pitfall: Rebuild the completer when tools change — a fixed list omits dynamically registered tools.

examples.title: Persist history across sessions
examples.intent: Keep command history between runs.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: FileBackedHistory writes to the data-local history file, so the learn stage carries prior operator intent forward into future loops.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the history node shows the persisted command log across sessions.
touch_interaction.visual: A timeline of past commands scrolls, grouped by session date.

examples.mini_scenario: Restarting selfware, the operator flicks up and recalls yesterday's build command instantly.
examples.pitfall: Ensure the history parent dir exists (create_dir_all) or persistence silently fails.
